acceptance: Measure queue depth and wait per workflow for one week; identify runs that add no signal (superseded heads, duplicate extension-smoke, cancelled-but-queued) and add concurrency cancellation or path filters; decide on runner capacity. Report median core wait before and after.
context:
2026-10-31 evidence (session on CI time): the queue is mostly CI, not oracle. A CI run executes about 22 jobs and about 4,300 runner-seconds per pull-request event; oracle work uses about 2 runner-minutes per event, so CI is about 97% of runner time. Between 11:23 and 15:17 UTC there were 122 pull-request events against 8 develop pushes, with 54 open pull requests. By run count about 125 of 205 queued runs were oracle workflows, but they take almost no runner time. The queue drained to 0 by 2026-11-01 13:06 UTC. Editing oracle workflows to shrink it was reviewed and judged unsafe (see oracle-gate-bridge-noop-runs-hold-runner-slots-20261101). Options with no gate risk: cap open pull requests or concurrent pushes, avoid ready_for_review in the same second as a push (oracle-verdict-same-second-push-and-ready-cancels-new-head-20261101), and reduce ci.yml fan-out (ci.yml is a soundness path). The owner chose not to change runner capacity; the Free plan pool is 20 jobs.

2026-11-11: merged duplicate throwaway-workflows-starve-required-ci-20261101 into this item. Contributor from that item: on 2026-10-31 a throwaway release-UAT dry run (run 41163626947, branch ci/release-uat-dryrun) held about 15 parallel jobs for hours while 100+ required runs queued. Candidate remedy: a concurrency cap for experimental workflows (max-parallel, separate runner group, or off-hours schedule).

Revalidated 2026-11-11: still required; the acceptance (one week of per-workflow queue measurement, removal of no-signal runs, runner-capacity decision, before/after core wait) has not been delivered. Current state: on 2026-11-11 evening 19 workflow runs were queued and 21 in progress repository-wide (down from 197 queued on 2026-10-31); a sample of recent ci.yml test jobs showed a median queue wait near zero and a maximum under 1 minute, so the multi-hour waits are now intermittent bursts rather than constant. ci.yml already has a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true (ci.yml:14-16), so superseded-head cancellation exists; the remaining candidates are the experimental-workflow concurrency cap and fan-out reduction. First-pass CI is also poor, which multiplies queue load: of the latest 100 pull_request ci.yml runs (2026-11-10 to 11-11), 40 succeeded on attempt 1, 13 failed and 14 were cancelled on attempt 1, and 19 needed 2 or more attempts (see rv2r-10-flaky-ci-investigation). No ruleset or runner-capacity change since 2026-10-31 (owner chose not to change capacity). Priority left unchanged.

Correction to the 2026-11-11 revalidation note: the number of ci.yml pull_request runs needing 2 or more attempts is 26 of the latest 100 (not 19); 6 more were still running on attempt 1.
description: Observed 2026-10-31: 59-128 queued workflow runs with 1-6 in progress; later 197 queued and 0 in progress at 15:32Z, oldest queued run from 11:50Z. pr-arm refuses until core records the verify-fast-duration verdict, so each push (including GitHub "Update branch" merges, which also restart oracle review) restarts a multi-hour wait. Six release-UAT fix PRs took from about 07:30Z to 14:11Z to merge once their CI was fixed; later fixes waited 5+ h more. Queue contributors include about 30 concurrent QuestDB PRs from one session and per-PR oracle and extension-smoke runs.
